title.full: ASEAN Green Future Project Phase 2.1 & 2.2 Report, Modeling Myanmar's path to a Near-Zero Emissions Power sector by 2050

publisher.full: Sustainable Development Solutions Network and ClimateWorks Centre

description: Myanmar-specific high ambition near-zero emissions pathway.
pathwayDescription:
The ASEAN Green Future regional research project is run by the United Nations Sustainable Development Solutions Network, Climateworks Centre, and local researchers from leading universities. The project develops national policy analysis and near-zero pathways that are meant to provide policy recommendations and support policy makers.

The Optimized More Ambitious Pathway (OMAP) is a normative, least-cost decarbonization scenario for Myanmar that seeks to achieve near-zero power-sector emissions by 2050. This scenario is complemented by the Existing Policy Pathway (EPP)—a scenario which reflects achieving current policy objectives in Myanmar—and the Optimized Existing Policy Pathway (OEPP)—a scenario with the same assumptions as the Existing Policy Pathway, but constructed using a cost optimization module.

OMAP builds on the same socio-economic foundation as the EPP and OEPP scenario, but applies stringent emissions constraints, accelerated electrification, and enhanced efficiency measures. On the supply side, OMAP shifts decisively away from fossil fuels, restricting additions of new thermal capacity and limiting expansion of large hydropower, due to existing challenges with hydropower in the region. The pathway instead prioritizes major growth in solar, biomass, geothermal, and energy-storage technologies, with capacity expansion optimized using a Next Energy Modeling Optimization (NEMO) module to meet demand reliably at the lowest system cost under the high-ambition constraint. NEMO is an open-source energy system optimization tool developed by the Stockholm Environment Institute. 

Electricity demand rises substantially as economic activity grows and electrification expands across households, transport, and industrial sectors. Urbanization increases energy service needs while efficiency gains moderate demand growth relative to economic activity. Full access to electricity is reached early in the modeling period, supporting broader social and economic development.

coreDrivers.policies: The scenario includes more ambitious targets for electricity demand. Fossil Fuel capacities are progressively phased out and low carbon technology additions are optimised based on NEMO optimization tools.
coreDrivers.emissionsTargets: OMAP aims to achieve near-zero emissions from electricity generation by 2050, by introducing constraints to limit the use of fossil fuels.
coreDrivers.technologyCosts: Technology capital, O&M and fuel costs affect least-cost capacity choices. Low-carbon technology should replace high carbon power generation, and the selection of technology is made based on technology costs.
coreDrivers.macroeconomicDrivers: Follows SSP2. GDP and medium population growth extracted from World Bank data, combined with stronger electrification and efficiency assumptions this drives electricity demand growth. The demand growth is much more signififcant than the forecasted in other pathways. Electricity demand, for example, is twice as high in 2050 in this pathway than in the EPP and OEPP pathways.

dependencies.dependency_description: The pathway assumes significantly more electrification and power demand by 2050. Current policies are not enough and cost optimisation is used to maximise investment costs while still filling demand.
The pathway plans some important increase in electricity demand. Power additions are not enough to meet demand, and 14% of electricity needs in Myanmar comes from import in 2050.
Local opposition to large hydropower already stricked in Myanmar. This scenario is more using solar potential in Myanmar due to cost efficiency and is not planning any hydro addition in Myanmar.
Adoption of efficient appliances, electric cooking, EVs and electrified industrial processes substantially raises electricity demand while reducing demand-side emissions.
OMAP requires 9 GW batteries to maintain the reserve margin at a safe level above 30%. It also accounts for 3 GW imports and diversified firm generation by 2050.
As solar expansion is important in this scenario, this scenario also highly rely on battery storage, reaching 9GW of battery storage by 2050.
OMAP nearly exhausts modeled solar and geothermal potentials. It therefore doesn't build out any hydro capacity, limiting risks from breakdown due to more severe droughts.
Drought and climate variability threaten hydropower reliability. Biomass is also important in the pathway with 5GW required by 2050, on the 6GW of technical potential assessed in Myanmar.
